question: Who among the following received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1936 for ‘studying the molecular structure through the investigation of dipole moments and the diffraction of X-rays and electrons in gases’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Peter Debye**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Peter Debye**

__
 
• **Peter Debye was the Dutch chemist who best knows his work on X-ray diffraction and dipole moments.**
 
• Some of his notable works are the Debye model, Debye relaxation, Debye frequency, Debye–Huckel equation, Debye-Waller factor​ , etc.
 
• He was the recipient of the **Nobel prize in the year 1936 for his work on X-ray diffraction and dipole moments.**
 
• The magnitude of the dipole moment is given in Debye units to honor him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** ​Arnold Sommerfeld**

 
• Arnold Sommerfeld was a **German physicst. **
 
• He investigated the atomic spectra of the Bohrs Model and concluded that the orbits of electrons in atoms are elliptical.
 
• **The nucleus is one of the foci of this ecliptical path.**
 
• He also introduced the ideas of Azimuthal and magnetic quantum numbers. 

**Paul Hermann Scherrer **

 
• Paul Hermann Scherrer was a **Swiss physicist.**
 
• **In 1916, while still working on his dissertation, he and his tutor, Peter Debye, developed the “Debye–Scherrer powder method”, a procedure using X-rays for the structural analysis of crystals.**
 
• This made an important contribution to the development of the scattering techniques that are still used in the large facilities at the Paul Scherrer Institute to this day.

**Erich Huckel**

 
• Erich Armand Arthur Joseph Huckel was **a German physicist and physical chemist.**
 
• He is known for two major contributions:
 
 
• The** Debye–Huckel theory of electrolytic solutions.**
 
• The Huckel method of approximate molecular orbital calculations on π electron systems.
